verdicts.justification: Reproduced all four legs. hyp.cluster(X(300,5), cluster='FeatureAgglomeration', n_clusters=3) returned 5 labels: 'cluster() label count on (300,5): 5 labels: [2, 0, 0, 1, 0]' -- vs docstring line 197 'a list of cluster labels (one per observation)'. plot dict k=2 silently drew 3 of 300 rows: real point-artists [1, 2] (six 1-point legend/axis proxies aside), and the evidence PNG plot_featureagglomeration_k2_silent_drop.png shows exactly 3 points in an empty cube. plot default: 'ValueError: Cannot extract more clusters than samples: 5 clusters were given for a tree with 3 leaves.' Reuse: 'NotImplementedError: FeatureAgglomeration has no out-of-sample prediction (no predict method); cannot reuse a fitted FeatureAgglomeration clusterer on new data (a different number of rows than it was fit on) without refit' -- raised even on the SAME data it was fit on (5 labels != 300 rows).

All four models crash identically: 'DBSCAN RAISED TypeError: DBSCAN.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'n_clusters'' (same for MeanShift, OPTICS, AffinityPropagation), while HDBSCAN alone gets the friendly path: 'HDBSCAN OK; warnings: [n_clusters is not a valid parameter for HDBSCAN clustering and will be ignored.]'. plot.py lines 1909-1918 special-case only HDBSCAN and mixture models before injecting n_clusters into params.

Confirmed behaviorally and in source. With a grouping metric that captures the line artists plot actually draws, the auditor's exact repro data gave 'auditor data seeded: distinct groupings over 3 runs: 3' -- three random_state=0 calls produced three different cluster groupings. On a second dataset, seeded and unseeded behaved identically (4 distinct groupings over 4 runs each), and unseeded KMeans on plot's own xform_data gave 6 distinct partitions in 6 runs while hyp.cluster(..., random_state=0) on the same xform was stable -- so the non-determinism is exactly the missing seed. Source: plot.py:1922 calls clusterer(xform, cluster={'model': model, 'kwargs': params}) with no random_state (line 1956 likewise), while the plot docstring (plot.py:612-616) promises random_state 'is injected into any stage model whose constructor accepts a random_state (UMAP, TSNE, KMeans, GaussianMixture, ...)'. Note: naive re-runs of the auditor's repro can spuriously look reproducible if the comparison only reads mpl collections (points render as Line3D), which initially misled this verification.

Reproduced: hyp.plot(data, '.', cluster='KMeans', return_model=True) drew 5 groups (real point-artists sizes [44, 56, 100, 62, 38] via default_params KMeans n_clusters=5) but 'pipeline transform unique k: 3' -- the returned pipeline's cluster stage was built with hyp.cluster's default n_clusters=3, so pipeline.transform cannot reproduce the plotted grouping.

Reproduced numerically: int cluster labels as hue give facecolors [(0.86, 0.34, 0.34, 1.0), (0.86, 0.371, 0.34, 1.0)] -- two reds differing by 0.031 in one channel, visually indistinguishable. String labels give clearly distinct colors [(0.34, 0.829, 0.86), (0.86, 0.371, 0.34)]. Evidence verbatim_plot_clusters2.png shows the shipped examples/plot_clusters2.py (which passes hyp.cluster int labels straight to hue=, lines 26-29) rendering two well-separated clusters in a single uniform red; hue_int_labels_k3_collision.png shows clusters 0 and 1 in the same red at k=3.
